name: Netherlands

facts.religion: No religion about 58%, Catholic about 17%, Protestant about 13%, Muslim about 5%

snapshot: Rob Jetten became the Netherlands' youngest and first openly gay prime minister in February 2026, after his D66 overtook Geert Wilders' far right.
culture: The Dutch Golden Age gave the world Rembrandt and Vermeer, and Van Gogh followed. Cycling is the main way to get around, and King's Day turns the country orange. The Dutch are known for directness, pragmatism and early liberal laws on drugs, euthanasia and same-sex marriage, which it was first to legalise, in 2001.
society: Rotterdam is Europe's largest port, and ASML, maker of the machines that print advanced chips, is one of Europe's most valuable companies. A severe housing shortage, nitrogen pollution limits on farming and migration fuelled the rise of Wilders and the farmers' party. A quarter of the country lies below sea level.
situation: In 2023 Geert Wilders, the Netherlands' most prominent anti-Islam politician, won an election for the first time. His coalition, the most right-wing in modern Dutch history, lasted 11 months before he pulled out over asylum laws, triggering a snap election in October 2025. This time the winner, by a narrow margin decided only after postal ballots were counted, was the centrist D66 under Rob Jetten.

On 23 February 2026, Jetten was sworn in at 38 as the Netherlands' youngest prime minister and its first openly gay one (AP via WTOP). His coalition with the centre-right VVD and Christian Democrats is something new for the Dutch: a minority government, holding just 66 of 150 seats with no formal outside support, so every law needs votes from the opposition (HSS). Wilders's PVV came second but every coalition party ruled him out. Jetten promised to bring the Netherlands "back to the heart of Europe," keep up support for Ukraine and raise defence spending, but his coalition also announced deep cuts to welfare and health care and kept much of the previous government's immigration line. After four elections since 2017, the Dutch are testing whether a deliberately consensual style can outlast the fragmentation that brought Wilders to power.
power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. The prime minister needs the confidence of the 150-seat House of Representatives, elected by nationwide proportional representation with almost no threshold, which produces many parties; the indirectly elected Senate can block laws.
holders: Prime Minister Rob Jetten (D66), in office since 23 February 2026.
